SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.37
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical pattern of a mono-substituted benzene: very strong ring-breathing at 1000 cm⁻¹, paired C=C stretches at 1589/1604 cm⁻¹ and a set of CH out-of-plane bends near 675, 760 and 785 cm⁻¹.  Candidate 1 fits this substitution pattern (only one phenyl substituent).  
The substituent must be an epoxide:  • a strong band at 1028 cm⁻¹ and another at 1245 cm⁻¹ correspond to the characteristic C–O–C asymmetric and symmetric stretches of an oxirane ring;  • the epoxide ring deformation appears at 894 cm⁻¹, and a second C–O–C vibration at 838 cm⁻¹ is also expected for phenyl-substituted oxiranes.  
Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2971 and 2879 cm⁻¹ are consistent with the two CH₂ groups of the oxirane, while the aromatic C–H stretch at 3073 cm⁻¹ matches the benzene ring.  
No strong S=O (≈1140/1300 cm⁻¹) or C–Cl (≈600-700 cm⁻¹) bands are present, arguing against the sulfone- or chloro-containing alternatives (candidates 2, 4, 8, 9, 10).  
Thus the overall peak set—mono-substituted phenyl features plus distinctive epoxide C–O–C bands—best matches phenyl-oxirane, i.e. candidate 1 (c1ccc(C2CO2)cc1).
